newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslavia to seek contacts with IMF - deputy PM.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia to seek contacts with IMF - deputy PM.

text.p: Yugoslavia will do whatever is necessary to urgently renew contacts with world financial institutions and creditors and hopes to make some progress by the end of 1997, a federal official said on Monday.

"Yugoslavia's return to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank will be the top priority of this government in 1997," the newly-appointed Yugoslav Deputy Prime Minister Danko Djunic told Reuters.
The Deputy PM insisted Belgrade authorities were ready to talk any time and any place about all issues concerning Yugoslavia's return to the IMF and World Bank.
"Tomorrow, I'll be ready to go to the North Pole if necessary to talk to those institutions," Djunic said.
"We will do whatever is up to us," Djunic said but stopped short of saying Yugoslavia was accepting all the demands by the IMF to rejoin its membership.
Yugoslavia has been banned from financial institutions since 1992 when crippling U.N. sanctions imposed in May isolated the country from the international community.

Sanctions were lifted last October but an outer wall of sanctions remained in place barring the country from the IMF and the World Bank and foreign funds urgently needed to revive its moribund economy.

Belgrade's return to the IMF was conditional on its cooperation with the Hague war crimes tribunal, respect for human rights in its mostly-Albanian southern Kosovo province and progress in talks on dividing former Yugoslavia's assets.

Rejoining the IMF, World Bank, World Trade Organisation and renewing contacts with Yugoslav creditors were seen as crucial for the country's economic development and its reintegration into the world economy.
The IMF board of directors postponed any discussion on Yugoslavia's membership until June 14.

"Considering our situation, June 14 is very far away. But we shall not wait until June 14, we shall not even wait for April 14, we shall start immediately," Djunic told a news conference. But he did not say what or how.
In order to improve its image and revive contacts with world financial bodies, the government decided to launch a new IMF ministry in its latest cabinet reshuffle.

"Right now, being new to the government, we have to look at what our predecessors left us and into all problems. But very soon, we shall draft a programme of all necessary activities and form a work group. We shall try to separate technicalities from politics," Djunic told a news conference.

"But whether there will be contacts is not entirely up to us. We will do all we can. We hope that creditors will also do their part of the job professionally. We are ready for those contacts, there is an initiative from Belgrade, but there is no response yet." -- Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
